en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-caurapraśamanī-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court-Dispersing Grandee, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Magadha,
walking to and fro surrounded by a great assembly.
They arrived at the side of the Āmra Grove, within the Śakrakaṇḍaka Cave on Mount Vaidehī.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda suddenly saw a great multitude of fierce robbers approaching from afar.
Having seen this, he was seized by great terror;
his mind was filled with distress and his hair stood on end.
Then, the Venerable Ānanda went quickly to where the Buddha was.
Having arrived, he joined his palms and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I now see from afar a great and evil bandit.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will provide protection and deliverance."
At that time, having heard the words of the Venerable Ānanda, the World-Honored One said to Ānanda, "Are you afraid of the bandits?
Ānanda replied to the Buddha, "I am very much afraid, World-Honored One."
The Buddha said, "Ānanda, do not be afraid.
I have a dhāraṇī that can eliminate the danger of bandits.
At that time, having heard the Buddha's words, the Venerable Ānanda felt great joy in his heart.
He spoke these words: "I pray only that the World-Honored One will proclaim it for me.
At that time, the World-Honored One then recited the Great Wheel Boundary-Dhāraṇī, saying:

*Tadyathā:* 1. *Āṅgulike* 2. *Prarupe* 3. *Ikā-atipatye* 4. *Aurī-ghaṇḍarī* 5. *Caṇḍarī* 6. *Mātangi* 7. *Jāyuri* 8. *Pukkasie* At that time, having spoken this dhāraṇī, the World-Honored One [ceased].
He addressed the Venerable Ānanda: "You should now go and,
by means of this dhāraṇī,
establish a boundary for twelve yojanas in every direction."
It shall cause them to attain peace and security, extinguishing the calamities of bandits;
even swords, blades, and weapons shall be unable to harm them.
Furthermore, it shall also cause those wicked bandits to—
Without leaving its original position, it rotates like a potter’s wheel.
Furthermore, Ānanda, if a person encounters the danger of bandits,
they should use pure white thread.
By empowering this dhāraṇī seven times and tying it into seven knots,
one passes through difficulties and they are immediately released.
All bands of thieves will be as if bound under restraint and will be unable to cause harm.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra,
the Venerable Ānanda and the great assembly,
having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sutra on the Dhāraṇī for Quelling the Peril of Robbers Spoken by the Buddha.
